original_question: Let (A, A) be a maximal Banach ideal. Call (A, A) right-accessible when, for every finite-dimensional Banach space E, Banach space Y, operator T in L(E, Y), and epsilon > 0, there exist a finite-dimensional subspace N of Y and S in L(E, N) such that T factors through N and A(S) <= (1 + epsilon) A(T). Is this right-accessibility property equivalent to the A-local reflexivity principle for maximal Banach ideals?
target_in_paper: Section 1, Problem 1.5: for a maximal Banach ideal (\mathfrak A,\mathbf A), is right-accessibility equivalent to satisfying the \mathfrak A-local reflexivity principle? The surrounding paper-faithful context is Definition 1.1 (\mathfrak A-LRP), Definition 1.3 (right-/left-accessibility), Proposition 1.4 (right-accessible => \mathfrak A-LRP), and Theorem 1.8 (\mathfrak A-LRP <=> left-accessibility of the conjugate ideal \mathfrak A^\Delta).
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the main open problem the note isolates: the setting of maximal Banach ideals, the right-accessibility condition, and the question whether that condition is equivalent to the \mathfrak A-local reflexivity principle. This is exactly the content of Problem 1.5, with Proposition 1.4 supplying one direction.
missing_details: The paper’s official target is Problem 1.5, not the broader Problem 1.2; the refined question should explicitly say it is asking whether two properties are equivalent for every maximal Banach ideal.
The notation should distinguish the ideal from its norm, as in (\mathfrak A,\mathbf A), rather than writing the same symbol twice.
The ambient scalar field is the usual Banach-space field \mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}; the paper treats Banach spaces in the standard real/complex setting.

Right-accessibility should be written with the canonical inclusion J_N^F:N\hookrightarrow F and the factorization identity T=J_N^F S, where M is finite-dimensional, F is arbitrary, N\in FIN(F), S\in \mathfrak L(M,N), T\in \mathfrak L(M,F), and \varepsilon>0.
The draft names the \mathfrak A-local reflexivity principle but does not define it. In the paper this is essential context from Definition 1.1.
In the \mathfrak A-LRP, the operator to be lifted is T\in \mathfrak A(M,F''), not merely an arbitrary operator M\to F or M\to F''.
The \mathfrak A-LRP includes a finite-dimensional test space N\in FIN(F') and the pairing condition \langle Sx,b\rangle=\langle b,Tx\rangle for all x\in M and b\in N.
The \mathfrak A-LRP also includes the canonical embedding condition j_F Sx=Tx for every x\in M with Tx\in j_F(F); this is missing from the draft.
Because Proposition 1.4 already proves right-accessible => \mathfrak A-LRP, the unresolved content is the converse implication; the refined question should reflect that paper context.
Theorem 1.8 gives an explicit reformulation of the \mathfrak A-LRP via left-accessibility of the conjugate ideal \mathfrak A^\Delta, which is the only paper-sanctioned alternate formulation nearby.
refined_question: Let (\mathfrak A,\mathbf A) be a maximal Banach ideal over \mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}. Is the following equivalence always true? (i) (\mathfrak A,\mathbf A) is right-accessible, meaning that for every finite-dimensional Banach space M, every Banach space F, every T\in \mathfrak L(M,F), and every \varepsilon>0, there exist N\in FIN(F) and S\in \mathfrak L(M,N) such that T=J_N^F S and \mathbf A(S)\le (1+\varepsilon)\mathbf A(T). (ii) (\mathfrak A,\mathbf A) satisfies the \mathfrak A-local reflexivity principle, meaning that for every finite-dimensional Banach space M, every Banach space F, every N\in FIN(F'), every T\in \mathfrak A(M,F''), and every \varepsilon>0, there exists S\in \mathfrak L(M,F) such that \mathbf A(S)\le (1+\varepsilon)\mathbf A(T), \langle Sx,b\rangle=\langle b,Tx\rangle for all x\in M and b\in N, and j_F Sx=Tx for every x\in M with Tx\in j_F(F)?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, using Theorem 1.8, for every maximal Banach ideal (\mathfrak A,\mathbf A), is right-accessibility of (\mathfrak A,\mathbf A) equivalent to left-accessibility of its conjugate ideal (\mathfrak A^\Delta,\mathbf A^\Delta)?
justification: The draft is aiming at the paper’s exact open equivalence question, namely Problem 1.5 in Section 1. Definition 1.3 in the note matches your right-accessibility clause, Proposition 1.4 establishes the forward implication from right-accessibility to the \mathfrak A-local reflexivity principle, and Theorem 1.8 identifies the \mathfrak A-LRP with left-accessibility of the conjugate ideal. What your draft lacked was the full stand-alone Definition 1.1 of the \mathfrak A-LRP, especially the bidual target T\in \mathfrak A(M,F''), the finite-dimensional testing subspace N\subset F', and the canonical embedding condition on points already lying in j_F(F).
